title: The Cloud & Branch Connector Dashboard: Traffic Monitoring widgets, Geo View, monitoring table and Traffic Flow

prose.label: Widgets.
prose.text: {{throughput-widget}} {{sessions-widget}} {{geo-view}} No refresh cadence or retention is given for the widgets, and the time filter's default and range are not given {{gap:widget-time-range}}.

prose.label: Traffic Flow.
prose.text: {{traffic-overview}} {{total-traffic}} What "inbound" means in the Tx Bytes definition is open {{gap:tx-bytes-definition}}. {{drill-to-logs}}

prose.label: DNS.
prose.text: {{dns-overview}} The rule and its actions are in [[cloud-connector.dns.policies]].

checks.do: For DNS traffic handled by the DNS Filtering Rule, the DNS Monitor's blocked and resolved-by-Private-Access counts, with the rule's actions in the DNS policies subject.

scope.statement: The Traffic Monitoring page of the Dashboard shows the name, group, location, throughput and session data across services of a Cloud or Branch Connector, and a Refresh icon refreshes the dashboard to the most recent information.

quotes: The Traffic Monitoring page provides information on the name, group, location, throughput, and session data across services of your Cloud or Branch Connector.
You can use the Refresh icon () to refresh the dashboard to view the most recent information

location-filters.statement: Cloud Connectors can be filtered under AWS Regions, Azure and GCP and Branch Connectors under Branch Connector Locations; the filter is Any by default, which means no filter is applied.

quotes: You can filter Cloud Connectors under AWS Regions, Azure, and GCP. You can filter Branch Connectors under Branch Connector Locations.
By default, the filter is set to Any which indicates that no filter is applied.

throughput-widget.statement: The Throughput Across Services chart displays the throughput of traffic flowing through Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), Direct, and Log & Control, in Mbps.

quotes: The Throughput Across Services chart displays all the throughput of the traffic flowing through Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA), Zscaler Private Access (ZPA), Direct, and Log & Control
The throughput across services is displayed in Mbps.

sessions-widget.statement: The Sessions Across Services chart displays the session count data of ZIA, ZPA, Direct, and Log & Control.

quotes: The Sessions Across Services chart displays all the session count data of ZIA, ZPA, Direct, and Log & Control

geo-view.statement: Clicking a cluster in the Geo View shows the Cloud and Branch Connectors in a region with their cloud provider type (AWS, Azure, GCP, Branch Cloud), and clicking a connector shows its throughput and session count data.

quotes: You can click the cluster to view all the Cloud and Branch Connectors in a particular region along with their cloud provider type (i.e., AWS, Azure, GCP, Branch Cloud).
You can also click any Cloud and Branch Connector to view its throughput and session count data.

monitoring-table.statement: The monitoring table lists, for each connector, the throughput and session data forwarded through ZIA, through ZPA and directly, and its View icon opens the Traffic Flow page.

quotes: ZIA (Throughput/Session): The throughput and the session data that are forwarded through the Internet & SaaS (ZIA) cloud.
ZPA (Throughput/Session): The throughput and the session data that are forwarded through the Private Access (ZPA) cloud.
Direct (Throughput/Session): The throughput and the session data that are forwarded directly.
Click the View icon to access the Traffic Flow page

traffic-overview.statement: The Traffic Flow page's Session Count Trend lists the session count across the Internet & SaaS, Private Access, Direct, Log & Control GW, and total services, and a Log & Control GW figure gives the session count forwarded through the Log and Control gateway.

quotes: Log & Control GW: The session count data forwarded through the Log and Control gateway.
The Session Count Trend lists the session count across the Internet & SaaS, Private Access, Direct, Log & Control GW, and total services

total-traffic.statement: The Traffic Flow page defines Rx Bytes as the number of inbound bytes received by the service per second and Tx Bytes as the number of inbound bytes transmitted by the service per second.

quotes: Rx Bytes: Displays the number of inbound bytes received by the service per second.
Tx Bytes: Displays the number of inbound bytes transmitted by the service per second.

drill-to-logs.statement: Selecting a point on a Traffic Flow graph shows the value for that time period, and Click for more info displays the session logs, with real-time log consolidation for each transaction.

quotes: Select a point on the graph to see the value for the specified time period. Click for more info displays the session logs, where you can view real-time log consolidation for each transaction.

dns-overview.statement: The Traffic Flow page's DNS Monitor table displays data about the DNS traffic configured by the DNS Filtering Rule, with Block silently blocking matching requests and responses and Resolve by ZPA asking the connector to resolve requests using the Private Access IP pool; a DNS Transaction Trend lists transactions allowed, blocked or resolved by Private Access.

quotes: The DNS Monitor table displays data about the DNS traffic that is configured by the DNS Filtering Rule.
Block: Silently blocks all DNS requests and responses that match the rule.
Resolve by ZPA: Requests the Cloud or Branch Connector to resolve DNS requests using the Private Access IP pool.
The DNS Transaction Trend lists the transactions that are allowed, blocked, or resolved by Private Access

widget-time-range.title: Time range, refresh cadence and retention of the Dashboard widgets
widget-time-range.detail: The Traffic Flow page says the time and service filter can be adjusted using drop-down menus above each trend graph, but neither it nor the Traffic Monitoring page gives a default or range values for the time filter, a refresh cadence or retention for the widgets. The monitoring table lists ZIA, ZPA and Direct columns and no Log & Control column, an absence read from the page.
widget-time-range.blocks: saying how recent or how old a Dashboard figure is

tx-bytes-definition.title: What the Tx Bytes definition's "inbound" means
tx-bytes-definition.detail: The Traffic Flow page defines Tx Bytes as inbound bytes transmitted by the service per second, the same direction word as Rx Bytes. Whether that is a wording slip or a different measurement is not stated.
